results.evidence: BroadcastSummary.tsx renders `{canMoveToDraft && (<LemonButton ... onClick={revertBroadcastToDraft} ...>Move to draft</LemonButton>)}`. The listener `revertBroadcastToDraft` calls `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'draft' })` then `actions.saveBroadcastFinished(draft)` and `actions.setStep(values.firstInvalidStep ?? 'review')`. The `isReadOnly` selector is `!!broadcast && broadcast.status !== 'draft'`, so once status flips to 'draft' the wizard is no longer read-only and reopens on an editable step. A draft workflow's trigger is not active, so the scheduled send (tied to the workflow's active status) stops firing.

`canMoveScheduledBroadcastToDraft` returns false unless `broadcast.status === 'active'` (excludes drafts) and unless `(broadcast.schedules ?? []).some(schedule => schedule.status === 'active' || schedule.status === 'paused')` is true — an immediate send or a completed one-time schedule has no active/paused schedule row, so the function returns false and the button is hidden.

In `launchBroadcast`, `await deleteBroadcastSchedules(projectId, broadcastId, persisted?.schedules)` unconditionally removes every existing schedule (including a paused one) before activation. For 'later'/'recurring' mode a single `hogFlowsSchedulesCreate` call then creates exactly one new schedule (`activated = { ...activated, schedules: [createdSchedule] }`); for 'now' mode no schedule is created at all, so no leftover schedule remains that could fire later.

The sequence is `await deleteBroadcastSchedules(...)` then `activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` and only afterward, inside the schedule branch, `const createdSchedule = await hogFlowsSchedulesCreate(...)`. The broadcast is marked active *before* the new schedule is created, not after schedule replacement completes, so an interruption between activation and schedule creation can leave the broadcast live with zero schedules (mitigated only by a best-effort catch-block revert, not by ordering).

`canMoveScheduledBroadcastToDraft` only checks `broadcast.status`, batch job status (`waiting|queued|active`), and `batchJobsLoaded`; it never inspects `(broadcast.schedules ?? []).length` for 'more than one schedule' nor validates the workflow's action shape is one the wizard can safely edit. Both additional withholding conditions from the criterion are absent from the implementation.

The button's handler is wired directly: `onClick={revertBroadcastToDraft}` with no confirmation step, and the `revertBroadcastToDraft` listener immediately calls `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'draft' })` with no modal, `LemonModal`, or `window.confirm` gating it — there is no explicit confirm/cancel prompt before reverting.

`revertBroadcastToDraft` only performs `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'draft' })` and unconditionally shows `lemonToast.success('Broadcast moved to draft')` on success or a single generic error toast on failure. It never checks or cancels an in-progress batch job/run, and does not vary the message between 'nothing had started' vs 'a running send was cancelled' vs 'cancellation failed but broadcast is still draft'.

The entire patch touches only three frontend files (`BroadcastSummary.tsx`, `broadcastWizardLogic.ts`, `broadcastsLogic.ts`); no scheduler/backend code is modified to re-verify the broadcast's live status immediately before creating a send run, so nothing in this diff prevents the scheduler from starting a run for a broadcast concurrently moved out of live status.

The new schedule payload built in `launchBroadcast` only sets `rrule`, `starts_at`, and `timezone`: `const schedule: Partial<HogFlowScheduleApi> = { rrule: ..., starts_at: ..., timezone: values.effectiveTimezone }`. Neither `deleteBroadcastSchedules` nor the create call reads or forwards any variable-override field from the previous schedule, so such overrides would be dropped when the schedule is replaced.

result:
Scheduled broadcasts can be moved back to draft, and launching replaces any previous schedule with a new active one.

The broadcast summary stayed read-only after launch, so a scheduled send could not be stopped or edited from Broadcasts. The summary now shows Move to draft while the workflow is active, batch jobs have loaded, no send is in progress, and a schedule is still active or paused. That sets the workflow back to draft and opens the wizard on the first incomplete step (or review). A draft workflow does not fire, so the scheduled send stops and the details can be edited.

Relaunch was also leaving a paused schedule in place. Editing the audience pauses every active schedule, and schedule status is read-only, so that row can never be resumed. Launch now deletes existing schedules before activation, then creates one new schedule afterward. The new row is active, so the broadcast sends at the chosen time. Send now deletes old schedules too, so a leftover cadence does not also fire.

`canMoveScheduledBroadcastToDraft` covers when Move to draft is offered, including a schedule paused by an audience edit, and hides it while a send is in progress or batch jobs have not loaded.
